new.title: Admire the three eras of Saint-Sauveur Cathedral
new.desc: Aix's cathedral mixes Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque work, built on the Roman forum of Aquae Sextiae, with a baptistery from the early 6th century. The nave holds the Triptych of the Burning Bush by Nicolas Froment, commissioned by King René in 1476.
new.tip: Entry is free and the cloister is a quiet corner. The triptych is only on view at certain times, and visits pause during services.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Sauveur, Place des Martyrs de la Résistance, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Stroll the plane-lined Cours Mirabeau
new.desc: Ordered by the Parlement de Provence in 1649–1651 on the line of the old southern rampart, this 440 m avenue is lined with plane trees, four fountains and 17th and 18th century mansions. It separates the old town from the Quartier Mazarin.
new.tip: Walk it in the early evening and stop at a terrace; look for the Fontaine Moussue and the Fontaine des Neuf Canons.
new.q: Cours Mirabeau, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Step into Cézanne's last studio
new.desc: Paul Cézanne built this north-lit studio in 1902 and worked here until his death in 1906. His easel, palette and the still-life objects he painted are kept as he left them.
new.tip: About 20 minutes uphill from the centre. Visits are guided at set times and the studio closes in early January; check hours and book ahead.
new.q: Atelier de Cézanne, 9 Avenue Paul Cézanne, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Visit the Hôtel de Caumont art centre and garden
new.desc: This 18th century mansion in Aix, restored as an art centre since 2015, hosts two large temporary exhibitions a year in its salons. It has a garden and a café.
new.tip: Exhibitions change twice a year (Henri Cartier-Bresson until March 2027); check the programme and book tickets online.
new.q: Hôtel de Caumont Centre d'Art, 3 Rue Joseph Cabassol, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: See Cézanne and Granet at the Musée Granet
new.desc: Set in the former Priory of the Knights of Malta, the museum has works by Granet, Ingres, Picasso and a gallery of Cézanne. The ground floor holds Roman and Celto-Ligurian archaeology from Entremont.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll in the Mazarin quarter. Closed on Mondays; hours are shorter in winter.
new.q: Musée Granet, Place Saint-Jean-de-Malte, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Explore the optical art of Fondation Vasarely
new.desc: Victor Vasarely designed this building in 1976 with 16 hexagonal halls housing 44 giant integrations of his kinetic art. It is a landmark of op art in France.
new.tip: Allow about an hour. It is in the Jas-de-Bouffan district west of Aix; take a bus or drive, and check opening days.
new.q: Fondation Vasarely, 1 Avenue Marcel Pagnol, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Walk through the ochre Bibémus quarries
new.desc: These Aix stone quarries supplied the city's golden stone from Roman times. Cézanne painted them in the 1890s and rented a hut here. Visits are guided only.
new.tip: Visits are guided only; book through the Aix tourist office, tours run on set dates in season.
new.q: Carrières de Bibémus, Chemin de Bibémus, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Tour the Château de La Barben and its French garden
new.desc: This castle on a rock above the Touloubre valley has medieval origins and was remodelled in the 17th century, with a French-style garden. The interior is visited with a guide.
new.tip: Open daily from April to early November; access is through the Rocher Mistral park, so check prices and hours.
new.q: Château de La Barben, La Barben

new.title: Reach the Croix de Provence on Sainte-Victoire
new.desc: The 19th century cross crowns the summit of the limestone ridge painted by Cézanne in dozens of canvases. The views reach the Étang de Berre, Cassis and Mont Ventoux.
new.tip: Bring water; access is restricted in summer fire-risk periods and the last stretch is steep.
new.q: Croix de Provence, Montagne Sainte-Victoire, Saint-Antonin-sur-Bayon

new.title: Gaze at the turquoise Barrage de Bimont
new.desc: This arch dam in a limestone gorge below Sainte-Victoire was built from 1946 to 1951 and put into service in 1952. Its reservoir supplies the Aix branch of the Canal de Provence, and trails start from the car park.
new.tip: Swimming is prohibited. Park at the dam and walk the shore path.
new.q: Barrage de Bimont, Chemin du Barrage, Saint-Marc-Jaumegarde

new.title: Look up at the Roquefavour Aqueduct
new.desc: Built between 1841 and 1847 to carry the Canal de Marseille across the Arc valley, this three-tier stone aqueduct is about 82 m high and 393 m long. It stands between Ventabren and Aix.
new.tip: Trails and a picnic area sit beneath it; visit in the morning in summer.
new.q: Aqueduc de Roquefavour, Ventabren

new.title: Tour the Cistercian Abbaye de Silvacane
new.desc: Founded in 1144, this is one of the three Cistercian sisters of Provence with Thoronet and Sénanque. Its austere Romanesque church, cloister and chapter house are intact.
new.tip: Open year-round with seasonal hours, closed 25 December, 1 January and 1 May; it hosts concerts of the La Roque-d'Anthéron piano festival.
new.q: Abbaye de Silvacane, 183 Route de l'Abbaye, La Roque-d'Anthéron

new.title: Climb to the ruined Château de la Reine Jeanne in Ventabren
new.desc: This hilltop village overlooks the Arc valley and the Étang de Berre. The ruins of the Château de la Reine Jeanne, listed since 1989, crown the old town.
new.tip: Go at sunset for the views; park below the village and walk up the stairs.
new.q: Château de la Reine Jeanne, Ventabren

new.title: Eat Provençal aïoli at Les Galinas
new.desc: Les Galinas is a Provençal bistro in Aix awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025. Its menu centres on simple local recipes such as aïoli, raïto sauce and lamb tripe.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner; ask which Provençal classic is on the day's menu.
new.q: Les Galinas, 10 Rue Constantin, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Buy calissons at Pâtisserie Weibel near Place Richelme
new.desc: This family pâtisserie at the corner of Place Richelme (2 rue Chabrier) is called the most famous calisson house in Aix by Gault&Millau. It sells calissons, the almond and candied melon sweets of Aix, plus pastries.
new.tip: Pair a box of calissons with a market morning on the square.
new.q: Pâtisserie Weibel, 2 Rue Chabrier, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Taste calissons at Maison Béchard
new.desc: Maison Béchard, a family pâtisserie on Cours Mirabeau since 1870, is known for hand-made calissons d'Aix. Its other specialities include the Alexandre almond mousse and icing-sugar brioches, with a sit-down tea room.
new.tip: Try the calissons with a coffee; closed Sunday, check hours.
new.q: Maison Béchard, 12 Cours Mirabeau, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Shop for artisan calissons at Léonard Parli
new.desc: Léonard Parli has made calissons d'Aix since 1874 and holds the Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant label. The historic shop is at 35 avenue Victor Hugo, near La Rotonde.
new.tip: Open Monday to Saturday 9:30 to 19:00; buy a small box of calissons as a gift.
new.q: Léonard Parli, 35 Avenue Victor Hugo, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Visit the Roy René calisson factory and museum
new.desc: The Confiserie du Roy René has made calissons d'Aix and Provençal nougats since 1920. Its Musée du Calisson and shop are on the Route d'Avignon, with a free self-guided visit and paid guided tours.
new.tip: Guided tours need a reservation; the shop and museum are open daily.
new.q: Confiserie du Roy René, Musée du Calisson, 5380 Route d'Avignon, La Calade, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Dine on a Provençal terrace at La Taula in Villa Gallici
new.desc: La Taula is the restaurant of the Villa Gallici hotel, serving refined cooking that blends Provençal and Italian traditions in a flowered terrace garden. It is listed by the Michelin Guide and sits just outside the old town.
new.tip: Reserve a garden table for lunch or dinner.
new.q: La Taula Gallici, Villa Gallici, 18 Avenue de la Violette, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Dine at Le Saint-Estève in Le Tholonet
new.desc: Le Saint-Estève is the gastronomic restaurant of the Lodges Sainte-Victoire hotel at 2250 route Cézanne in Le Tholonet. The Michelin Guide lists it with one star, and the terrace overlooks the countryside.
new.tip: Book ahead; the same hotel's brasserie L'Atelier des Lodges is a cheaper alternative.
new.q: Le Saint-Estève, Les Lodges Sainte-Victoire, 2250 Route Cézanne, Le Tholonet

new.title: Eat a Provençal daube at Chez Thomé
new.desc: Chez Thomé, at La Plantation in Le Tholonet, is a Provençal institution for over fifty years, known for daube and pieds et paquets. It has a shaded summer terrace and a fireside room in winter.
new.tip: Closed Mondays and Sunday evening per listings; check before going, and pair with a walk to Barrage Zola.
new.q: Chez Thomé, La Plantation, Le Tholonet

new.title: Eat wood-fire Argentine grill at Francis Mallmann, Château La Coste
new.desc: Argentine chef Francis Mallmann cooks meat over open fire in this 90-seat restaurant on the Château La Coste estate, listed with a Michelin Plate. It is on the same grounds as the art walk.
new.tip: Open for lunch and dinner; reserve in advance.
new.q: Francis Mallmann au Château La Coste, 2750 Route de la Cride, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade

new.title: Taste local rosé at Les Vignerons du Mont Sainte-Victoire
new.desc: This cooperative cellar, built in 1924, groups about 80 growers farming around 700 hectares between Puyloubier and Sainte-Victoire. The cave sells and pours its Côtes de Provence rosé, red and white.
new.tip: Open Monday to Saturday 9:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 18:00 per listings; summer apéro evenings run with views of the mountain.
new.q: Les Vignerons du Mont Sainte-Victoire, 63 Avenue d'Aix, Puyloubier

new.title: Walk the Art and Architecture trail at Château La Coste
new.desc: Since 2011 this wine estate has hosted a walk through vineyards past works by Louise Bourgeois, Tadao Ando, Richard Serra, Alexander Calder and others. The art and architecture trail can be done self-guided or on a guided tour.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; allow about 2 hours and book tickets online.
new.q: Château La Coste, 2750 Route de la Cride, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade

new.title: Browse the Place Richelme produce market
new.desc: Aix's daily fruit and vegetable market fills Place Richelme from 8:00 to 13:00 with local produce, olive oil, goat's cheese, honey and herbs. Larger general markets run on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings elsewhere in the old town.
new.tip: Go in the morning, before 13:00.
new.q: Place Richelme, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Hike from Bimont dam to the Croix de Provence
new.desc: A classic climb from the Bimont dam car park by the Imoucha trail reaches the Prieuré de Sainte-Victoire at about 900 m, then the Croix de Provence. Allow 5 to 6 hours return.
new.tip: Start early; the Imoucha trail has been closed for works in the past and the Prieuré has restricted access, so check before going.
new.q: Parking du Barrage de Bimont, Saint-Marc-Jaumegarde

new.title: Walk the Tholonet circuit to the Zola and Roman dams
new.desc: A walking circuit from the centre of Le Tholonet passes the Roman dam ruins and the Barrage Zola, built in 1854 by François Zola, father of the writer Émile Zola. The area is Cézanne painting country.
new.tip: Fairly easy, about 2 to 3 hours. Check wildfire access rules in summer.
new.q: Parking du village, Le Tholonet

new.title: Climb the Pic des Mouches from Vauvenargues
new.desc: A long ridge route starts at Vauvenargues, follows the northern face of Sainte-Victoire to the Pic des Mouches (1,011 m) and reaches the Croix de Provence.
new.tip: A full-day walk for experienced hikers; carry plenty of water.
new.q: Parking des Cabassols, Vauvenargues

new.title: Taste Coteaux d'Aix wines at Château Henri Bonnaud
new.desc: This organic family estate in Le Tholonet offers a guided cellar visit followed by a tasting of its Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence cuvées, and a free walk through the vines.
new.tip: Book a visit; prices start around 15 euros and days vary.
new.q: Château Henri Bonnaud, 585 Chemin de la Poudrière, Le Tholonet

new.title: Tour the organic vineyards of Château de Calavon, Lambesc
new.desc: Château de Calavon is run by the Audibert family, winegrowers for five generations, near Lambesc. It offers a daily guided cellar visit with tasting of its organic wines.
new.tip: Book through the estate or the Aix tourism office; closed Monday per one listing.
new.q: Château de Calavon, 12 Avenue de Badonviller, Lambesc

new.title: See opera at the Festival d'Aix-en-Provence
new.desc: Founded in 1948, this international festival stages opera and concerts in July at the Théâtre de l'Archevêché (about 1,350 seats, open air) and the Grand Théâtre de Provence. The 2026 edition ran from 2 to 21 July.
new.tip: Tickets sell out months ahead; book at festival-aix.com.
new.q: Théâtre de l'Archevêché, Place des Martyrs de la Résistance, Aix-en-Provence

new.title: Follow the Cézanne footsteps trail in Aix
new.desc: Since 1990 bronze studs marked with a C set in the pavement link Cézanne's addresses on a walk of about 3 km through the old town. The route starts at the tourist office.
new.tip: Pick up the map at the tourist office on La Rotonde; allow half a day.
new.q: Office de Tourisme d'Aix-en-Provence, 300 Avenue Giuseppe Verdi, Aix-en-Provence
